findings.evidence: Rule check: 4 channel(s) not assigned to a sample: TMT132C, TMT133N, TMT133C, TMT134N. Description: "Four channels are unused."
findings.explanation: 12 samples occupy TMT126 to TMT132N of the 16-plex kit, leaving the last four channels empty. This matches the description (12 samples in a TMTpro 16-plex kit), so it is expected and harmless. Unused channels just carry no signal. The only analysis impact is slightly less multiplexing, and the empty channels should be excluded from normalization.
findings.suggested_fix: No change needed to the SDRF. Optionally note in the study documentation that TMT132C, TMT133N, TMT133C and TMT134N were intentionally left empty.

findings.evidence: Description: "RL cells (human diffuse large B-cell lymphoma cell line)"; SDRF characteristics[cell line]: HEK293 (while cellosaurus name is RL and accession is CVCL_1660)
findings.explanation: The cell line is given as HEK293, which contradicts the described RL DLBCL line. It also conflicts with the SDRF's own cellosaurus name (RL) and disease (diffuse large B-cell lymphoma). HEK293 is an embryonic kidney line, so this would mislead downstream reuse of the data.
findings.suggested_fix: Set characteristics[cell line] to RL in all rows, and check that the Cellosaurus accession matches RL.

summary: The one rule issue (4 unused TMT channels) is expected and matches the description. One real mismatch: characteristics[cell line] says HEK293 although the description, cellosaurus name and disease all indicate RL DLBCL cells.
